questions.question: Which query can a segment tree handle directly that a Fenwick tree cannot?
questions.explanation: A Fenwick tree answers ranges by subtracting prefixes, which needs an invertible operation. Min has no inverse, so a segment tree is used.

questions.question: In a range-minimum segment tree, what should a node completely outside the query range return?
questions.explanation: The value must be the identity for min, which is Infinity; returning 0 would corrupt answers for positive values.

questions.question: What does i & -i compute in a Fenwick tree?
options: The highest set bit of i
The number of set bits in i
The lowest set bit of i
questions.explanation: In two's complement, i & -i isolates the lowest set bit, which is the length of the block stored at index i. For 12 (binary 1100) it is 4.

questions.question: What problem does lazy propagation solve?
options: It builds the tree in O(1)
It makes range updates O(log n) instead of touching every leaf
questions.explanation: A lazy tag records a pending update on a fully covered node and pushes it to the children only when a later operation needs them.
